subroutines.name: install_driver
subroutines.title: Install the resident keypad driver
subroutines.description:
Enable the 50 Hz vertical-sync event and route it to the
matrix scanner. Sets User VIA port B to strobe the keypad (DDRB = &F0: top
nibble out, bottom nibble in) and hooks EVNTV to point at the event handler,
saving the previous vector at saved_evntv. Called from the BASIC front-end
via CALL &A00. Preserves all registers and flags (saved and restored around
the body).

subroutines.name: vsync_event_handler
subroutines.title: Vertical-sync event handler: scan the keypad
subroutines.description:
Entered from the MOS every 50 Hz vsync event. Strobes the
3x4 matrix through User VIA port B (bit 7 selects handset 0/1 via the 74LS157),
debounces and auto-repeats via debounce_counter, and on a pressed key sounds a
short key-click (OSWORD 7) and inserts the mapped character into the keyboard
buffer (OSBYTE &99). Every path exits through handler_exit, which restores the
registers and flags before chaining to the previous event vector, so all are
preserved (as the MOS event convention requires).

subroutines.name: main
subroutines.title: *RUN entry: relocate, decode, and auto-run
subroutines.description:
The file system execution address (*RUN entry-point) for this
binary. Relocates the whole image down to &0A00 (installing the resident driver
code and moving the encrypted BASIC to PAGE &0C00), decrypts the BASIC in place,
then queues 'PAGE=&C00 / OLD / RUN' so the now-plain BASIC front-end starts.

subroutines.name: decode_basic
subroutines.title: Decrypt the relocated BASIC
subroutines.description:
Rotate every byte of the relocated BASIC left one bit (the
inverse of the ROL-1 storage protection), across pages &0C00-&2AFF, in place.

subroutines.name: os_dependent_setup
subroutines.title: OS-version-dependent setup
subroutines.description: Reads os_signature to pick how the auto-run commands are queued.

subroutines.name: patch_basic_header
subroutines.title: Repair the BASIC program's first line
subroutines.description:
Write &16 (22) into basic_line10_len, the length byte of the
line-10 REM at PAGE=&0C00. That byte is stored as 0 (part of the protection),
so without this repair the relocated program cannot be LISTed or RUN.

subroutines.name: queue_autorun
subroutines.title: Queue the auto-run commands (direct poke)
subroutines.description:
Copy autorun_commands into the MOS keyboard buffer so the OS
reads them as typed and runs the decoded BASIC. autorun_index wraps into the
32-byte buffer at &03E0-&03FF.

subroutines.name: setup_keys
subroutines.title: Queue the auto-run commands (OSBYTE path)
subroutines.description:
The non-&4F-OS variant of queue_autorun: set the BREAK/ESCAPE
behaviour, then insert each autorun_commands byte with OSBYTE &8A.

subroutines.name: relocate_image
subroutines.title: Relocate the program image to &0A00
subroutines.description:
OSCLI the startup command, then block-copy the image from
&1900 down to &0A00 (copy_pages pages via copy_src -> copy_dst), skipping
destination page &0B so the soft-key buffer survives.

banners.name: softkey_buffer_image
banners.title: Soft-key buffer image (page &0B)
banners.description: Image of page &0B (the MOS soft-key/function-key buffer). The relocator skips page &0B so the user keys survive, making these bytes inert filler.

banners.name: basic_encoded
banners.title: Tokenised BASIC front-end (encoded)
banners.description: ROL-encoded tokenised BASIC (the keypad-definition editor); relocates to PAGE=&0C00 and is decrypted in place. Source: basic/voltmace-delta-14b-driver-keypad.bas.

banners.name: fossilised_memory
banners.title: Fossilised memory
banners.description: Uninitialised tail of the saved image. The file is a memory dump &1900-&3A80 (the BASIC clears exactly TO &3A80); the loader's code and tables end ~120 bytes short, so this holds whatever occupied the memory at save time. It is referenced by nothing and decodes as neither 6502, tokenised BASIC (raw or bit-rotated), nor text; its byte statistics are those of noise. Inert: the BASIC memory-clear overwrites it at startup.

memory_map.name: copy_dst
memory_map.description: Block-copy destination pointer used by the relocator.

memory_map.name: copy_src
memory_map.description: Block-copy source pointer used by the relocator.

memory_map.name: copy_rem
memory_map.description: Leftover (part-page) byte count for the relocator.

memory_map.name: decode_ptr
memory_map.description: ROL-decode cursor sweeping the encrypted BASIC in place.

memory_map.name: evntv
memory_map.description: EVNTV, the event vector: the resident driver saves the old value and points it at its vsync-event handler.

memory_map.name: autorun_index
memory_map.description: Running fill index into the keyboard buffer as the loader queues its PAGE / OLD / RUN commands.

memory_map.name: kbd_buffer
memory_map.description: Base of the &0300 page holding the MOS keyboard buffer (&03E0-&03FF), written directly on the fast hand-off path.

memory_map.name: basic_page
memory_map.description: PAGE the relocated BASIC runs at; the loader decrypts it in place here, then queues PAGE=&C00 / OLD / RUN.

memory_map.name: basic_line10_len
memory_map.description: Length byte of the relocated BASIC's line 10, patched from 0 back to &16 so the protected program lists and runs.

memory_map.name: os_signature
memory_map.description: OS ROM byte read (for 'O') to distinguish OS versions and choose the command hand-off path.

memory_map.name: user_via_orb_irb
memory_map.description: User VIA port B: writes column strobes and the 74LS157 handset-select bit (bit 7); reads the four matrix rows.

memory_map.name: user_via_ddrb
memory_map.description: User VIA data-direction register B: set to &F0 so the four strobe/select lines are outputs, the four rows inputs.

memory_map.name: osword
memory_map.description: OSWORD: the resident driver calls OSWORD 7 to sound the key-click.

memory_map.name: osbyte
memory_map.description: OSBYTE: A=&99 inserts a key into the buffer, A=&0E enables the vsync event, A=&8A inserts the loader's auto-run commands, and A=&C8 (200) sets the BREAK/ESCAPE effect.

memory_map.name: oscli
memory_map.description: OSCLI: issues the single startup command "T." (*TAPE) to select the cassette filing system; the PAGE/OLD/RUN commands instead go through the keyboard buffer.
